title: Robustness of periodicity in Grover walks under a magnetic vector potential
abstract: We study the effect of magnetic vector potentials on periodic Grover walks on finite graphs. The magnetic vector potential is introduced through the framework of quantum graphs, which induces the Grover walk as a special case. We regard the vector potential as a perturbation of a periodic Grover walk and investigate the robustness of its periodicity. Our analysis reveals that the response to such perturbations depends on the spectral structure of the underlying graph. In particular, when the graph possesses at least one non-simple eigenvalue, we derive a Hermitian matrix that characterizes the robustness of its periodicity. As a consequence, we show that the perturbed dynamics is asymptotically described by a continuous-time quantum walk generated by this Hermitian matrix.
summary: This paper analyzes how magnetic vector potentials perturb periodic Grover walks on finite graphs. By treating the potential as a small perturbation, the authors derive an effective continuous-time Hamiltonian $H$. The key finding is that the graph's spectral structure dictates the robustness of periodicity, providing quantitative measures for this stability.
main_problem: The study investigates how magnetic vector potential perturbations affect the periodicity of Grover walks executed on finite quantum graphs.
main_result: The perturbed dynamics can be shown to converge asymptotically to a continuous-time quantum walk generated by a Hermitian matrix $H$, whose spectral structure characterizes the robustness of the original periodicity.
method: The analysis employs spectral theory, treating the vector potential as a small perturbation ($ eta 	o 0$) and deriving an effective Hamiltonian $H$ from the discrete-time evolution operator.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum graph representing Grover walks on finite graphs ($P_n, C_n, K_{n,n}$). The dynamics are governed by a time evolution operator modified by a magnetic vector potential $ eta$.
key_observables: Periodicity ($	au$), Robustness of Periodicity ($R_p = \dim \ker H / |A|$), and the spectrum of the effective Hamiltonian $H$.
important_parameters: The perturbation strength $ eta$, which is assumed to be small; graph structure (e.g., presence of non-simple eigenvalues).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the underlying graph possesses at least one non-simple eigenvalue to derive the characterizing Hermitian matrix $H$. The convergence relies on the small-$ eta$ limit.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the perturbed walk dynamics, deriving the effective continuous-time Hamiltonian $H$, analyzing its spectral properties based on graph structure (e.g., path vs. cycle), and quantifying periodicity robustness using dimension counts ($\dim S_{	ext{sim}}, \dim T_{	ext{per}}, \dim L^{\perp}$).
why_interesting: This work connects fundamental concepts of quantum walks and graph theory to the stability of quantum dynamics under external fields, which is highly relevant for understanding decoherence or engineered robustness in quantum computation architectures.
